summary: This paper implements and simulates the quantum repeater with encoding and classical error correction (QRE-CEC) protocol in SeQUeNCe, extending the simulator with a stabilizer-based backend supporting CSS code operations and realistic noise models. The protocol distributes logical Bell pairs using Steane $\lfloor 7,1,3 \rfloor$ codes with encoded entanglement swapping and classical error correction for Pauli-frame corrections, achieving 0.91 fidelity over 2000 km while suppressing errors to second order.
motivation: Quantum repeaters must evolve toward distributing logical rather than physical entanglement as quantum networks move toward fault-tolerant operation, but the system-level interactions between heralded generation, encoding, idle decoherence, and classical error correction are difficult to evaluate analytically.
method: We extended SeQUeNCe with a tableau-based backend using Stim for efficient stabilizer simulation (memory scaling as $O(n^2)$ rather than $O(2^{2n})$), implemented CSS code operations, integrated five noise sources (one-qubit gate error $p_1^g$, two-qubit gate error $p_2^g$, measurement error $p_m$, idle decoherence with $T_1, T_2$ dependence, state initialization error), and simulated the five-phase QRE-CEC protocol including Barrett-Kok heralding, fault-tolerant state preparation via Paetznick–Reichardt 8-CNOT encoder with verification, transversal teleported CNOT, encoded swapping with Hamming-code syndrome decoding, and Pauli-frame correction.
result: QRE-CEC achieves second-order error suppression with fitted scaling exponent $c \approx 1.81$–$2.19$ consistent with $Q \sim q^2$; distributes logical Bell pairs with fidelity 0.91 at 2000 km (100 links with 20 km spacing) compared to 0.24 for unencoded QRE-None; and shows fidelity above 0.99 out to 100 km with latency 15–45 ms independent of correction overhead.
